title: Industry anatomy matrix
description: The industry a venture's market sits in, described on standard dimensions (Porter's five forces, regulation, cost of error, capital intensity, clockspeed) so that how strict its phase gates should be is derived from it rather than fixed (EE-157). Cells hold a value with status known, estimated or unknown (never null), cited evidence and when it was true. Kept per venture for now; shared across ventures in Mentura later.

id.description: Often the NAICS code, such as naics-541511

naics.description: The North American Industry Classification System code

cost_of_error.description: What a wrong product costs its user: reversible, costly, harmful or safety-critical

capital_intensity.description: low, medium or high: what it costs to build and run before revenue

time_to_revenue_days.description: Typical days from start to first revenue for a new entrant

clockspeed.description: slow, medium or fast: how fast products and processes change (Fine 1998)
